title: Keep the nightly report going past an uncalibrated sensor

blocks.text: The plant's nightly temperature report stops at the first sensor that has not been calibrated yet. The `Reading` record was written by another team: its `celsius()` refuses to hand out the value of an uncalibrated sensor, and also refuses a temperature below absolute zero, which only a broken feed can produce. The report prints nothing that night, and the morning shift has no temperatures at all.

items: an uncalibrated sensor gets the line `<sensor> uncalibrated`, for example `boiler-9 uncalibrated`, and the report goes on with the next event;
any other failure, a temperature below absolute zero included, still fails the report, and the reason it gives is the record's own.

blocks.text: Leave `Reading` and `line(...)` as they are: other reports use them. About six lines in total.

cases.says: with every sensor calibrated, the report has one line per event, in order
a reading whose record refuses its value as uncalibrated does not make the report fail
the uncalibrated sensor's line names it, and the events after it are still reported
a reading the record refuses for any other reason still fails the report, with that reason

origin.section: Matching Calls the Accessors, and an Exception From One Arrives as MatchException

concepts: An exception thrown by an accessor during a match arrives as MatchException with the original as its cause, so a catch for the original type misses it.
